description: End-to-end procedure for furnishing a book with a working clasp: preparing the metal catch, anchoring it in the boards, plaiting the leather strap, and dressing the leather around the fitting so the closed cover holds the leaves flat.
name: making and fitting a clasp

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (1901), Chapter XVIII, p.259. Internet Archive.
Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (D. Appleton, 1901), Internet Archive

steps.description: Shape the metal catch and ring from heavy silver wire, flattening the ends that will be buried in the board.
Anchor the catch: bed its flattened ends between the leaves of a double millboard and glue, or pass a turned end through a wooden board and rivet it on the inside.
Thread several thin leather strips through the ring, paste each strip's ends, and braid the doubled strips into a plait.
Lead the plait through a hole near the edge of the opposite board, set it into a cut groove and a scooped recess, and glue it down inside.
When covering, pierce the leather and work it carefully around the projecting catch so the fitting seats cleanly.
